claims.claim: 14-3-3 proteins bind phosphoserine-containing proteins through two motifs, RSXpSXP (mode 1) and RXY/FXpSXP (mode 2); the bound peptide is extended, with a tight turn at the pS+2 Pro (cis).
claims.source: Yaffe et al. 1997 Cell, PMID 9428519 (abstract read via Europe PMC)

claims.claim: 14-3-3 acts as a dimer; the dimer binds tandem phosphoserine motifs bidentately.
Structures of all seven human 14-3-3 isoforms bound to ligands; specificity determinants for phosphopeptide orientation in the amphipathic groove; domain flexibility.
claims.source: Yang et al. 2006 PNAS, PMID 17085597, PMC1859916 (abstract); the gamma entry from this work is 2B05 (inferred from release date and title, not checked)

claims.claim: 14-3-3 gamma residues R57 and R132 (native numbering) interact with the phosphoserine of the bound protein (input R56, R131).
LARP1 Ser548 is a recorded phosphosite; it is residue 7 (S7) of chain A (LARP1 542-552).

In the peptide PKGLSASLPDL only S7 is followed by X-Pro (S7-L8-P9), the pS-X-P core of both 14-3-3 motifs; S5 (S5-A6-S7) is not. No Arg at -3/-4 of S7 (L4, G3), so the peptide fits neither full consensus; K2 at -5.
claims.source: motif reading of PMID 9428519 against the FASTA, as counted here

claims.claim: 23 crystal/EM structures of human 14-3-3 gamma exist at 100% identity, most with bound phosphopeptides in the groove (e.g. 6S9K 1.60 A, 6ZBT 1.80 A, 6A5S 2.10 A).

not_known: No paper on the 14-3-3:LARP1 pS548 interaction or its structure was found (Europe PMC: '"LARP1" AND "14-3-3"', 'LARP1 AND Ser548', 'LARP1 AND (14-3-3 OR YWHA*)'); the organisers' description is not in the dossier, so whether the peptide was phosphorylated in the experiment is not confirmed here.
Which kinase phosphorylates LARP1 S548 was not read.
No team PDFs: /data/casp17/target_notes/H1388/papers/ does not exist.

decisions.chose: phosphoserine (SEP) on chain A residue 7 (LARP1 S548), af3 only, run next to the unmodified input
alternatives: unmodified only: rejected as the sole input, since 14-3-3 binding is phospho-dependent (PMID 9428519); kept as the control

decisions.chose: A1B1 (declared): one LARP1 phosphopeptide in the groove of one 14-3-3 gamma protomer; all five slate models A1B1
alternatives: A1B2 (dimer, one peptide): rejected, no tandem motif on an 11-mer to bind bidentately

decisions.chose: MSA: ColabFold MSA for chain B (14-3-3 gamma, 10,377 seqs, deep); chain A (11-mer LARP1 peptide) single-sequence (empty unpaired MSA), no paired MSA (a peptide has no pairable homologs). Same MSA set for every predictor.
alternatives: family crawl / plmMSA for the peptide: rejected, an 11-residue window carries no coevolution and its homologs would only repeat the motif
paired MSA: rejected, nothing to pair for a peptide

decisions.chose: Templates: chain B search templates (top 4) plus 6S9K chain A pinned at rank 1 (1.60 A, 100% id, phosphopeptide-bound groove) with --pin-template, since AF3 filters the >=95% identity hits; chain A none. No multimer template: no public 14-3-3:LARP1 complex, and threading the caspase-2 peptide would impose its register on a different sequence.
alternatives: multimer template from 6S9K/6ZBT with the foreign peptide: rejected, wrong sequence register; the groove pose is learned anyway
no templates: rejected, 23 exact-sequence structures exist and only help chain B
6ZBT or 6A5S pin: kept as fallback if 6S9K chain parsing fails

decisions.chose: PTM wiring: phosphoserine as an AF3/Protenix modification {ptmType: SEP, ptmPosition: 7} on chain A, added to the built input.json after residudes-engine inputs (the inputs CLI has no PTM flag; core AF3 folding_input and Protenix json_parser read ptmType). Boltz-2 and OF3 get the same SEP if their converters carry it, else they run unmodified and are labelled as such.
alternatives: phosphomimetic S7E: rejected, a weaker mimic of the dianionic phosphate that the K49/R56/R131/Y132 pocket recognises
SEP only, no unmodified control: rejected, the unmodified run tells whether the pose depends on the phosphate

decisions.chose: Sampling, all A1B1 (244 residues): af3 SEP 20 seeds x5 samples (lead arm); af3 unmodified 10 seeds x5 (control); protenix SEP 10 seeds x5; boltz-2 10 seeds x5; of3 10 seeds x5. ~60 seeds, ~300 models; estimate ~0.05 GPU-h per seed at this size, ~5 GPU-h with MSA/overhead, capped at 20 GPU-h of the 400 h budget. Selection gate: pS7 phosphate within 4 A of B K49/R56/R131/Y132 (input numbering); the gate decides, confidence ranks within a predictor. More seeds only if RESULTS_REVIEW finds the peptide register or direction split.
alternatives: 100+ af3 seeds up front: rejected, a small well-templated complex; loop:RUNNING if the pool splits
af3 only: rejected, predictor agreement on the groove pose is evidence
A2B2 dimer arm: rejected by D2, declared A1B1

decisions.chose: Slate v2: A1B1__sep__af3__s20_0, A1B1__sep__pt2__s5_0, A1B1__sep__af3__s9_0, A1B1__sep__pt2__s10_0, A1B1__sep__af3__s7_0. All pass the pocket gate and lie within 0.5 A (core A4-A10) of the af3+pS7/pt2 consensus; distinct seeds; af3+pS7 leads (C2)
alternatives: a bt2 hedge slot: bt2 gate-passing models split between ~3 A and ~12 A with no internal consensus
